content: 1. Efavirenz can increase the levels or effects of diazepam by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 2. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of buccal diazepam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of buccal diazepam by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Both buccal diazepam and efavirenz enhance sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Both intranasal diazepam and efavirenz increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of diclofenac by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Didanosine and efavirenz exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing each other's effects. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the risk of liver toxicity. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 10. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Estradiol valerate/dienogest should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuing the inducer. 11. Both difelikefalin and efavirenz increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of diltiazem by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Efavirenz and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz also reduces the levels or effects of disopyramide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 15. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of docetaxel by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Efavirenz and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 17. Efavirenz and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 18. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of dolutegravir by increasing its metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. If co-administered with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers, the dolutegravir dose should be increased to 50 mg twice daily. Close monitoring is required. 19. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of donepezil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of doravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 21. Efavirenz and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Efavirenz and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 26. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of duvelisib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 27. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of elacestrant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 28. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of elagolix by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix also decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of eletriptan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 31. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of eliglustat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is not recommended due to significant reductions in eliglustat exposure. 32. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 33. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced plasma concentrations and therapeutic failure. 34. Efavirenz and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of encorafenib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 36. Efavirenz and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of entrectinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 38. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide also reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 39. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 40. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It also increases erdafitinib levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 41. Efavirenz increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by decreasing their metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of vasospasm and ischemia. 42. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ergotamine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It also increases ergotamine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 43. Efavirenz and eribulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 44. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of erlotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative therapy is recommended. 46. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended.
